The Odyssey:
A classic told whole for children aged 4 to 7, from filmmaker Hugo Thomas, whose work has screened at Cannes and streams on Netflix: Homer's The Odyssey, from the Trojan Horse to the Cyclops and the Sirens, illustrated, in 40 pages and about ten minutes read aloud.

Odysseus wins a ten-year war with a wooden horse. Getting home takes him ten more years. A one-eyed giant eats his sailors like potato chips. A sorceress turns them into pigs. And when he finally reaches his island, a hundred strangers have moved into his palace and want to marry his wife.

He wrote it for his own five-year-old twins. These are the stories we all share. Meet them at five, and at fifteen they feel like old friends, not homework.

Adventures of Huckleberry Finn:
A classic novel told whole for children aged 4 to 7, from filmmaker Hugo Thomas, whose work has screened at Cannes and streams on Netflix: Mark Twain's Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, the raft, the Mississippi and the friendship of Huck and Jim, illustrated, in 40 pages and about ten minutes read aloud.

On the banks of the Mississippi lives a boy who sleeps in a barrel and jumps in every puddle. When his father comes back for his treasure, Huck makes everyone believe he is dead and slips away to an island. There he finds Jim, who has run away too: Jim is enslaved, and about to be sold far from his wife and children. The two friends set off on a raft, at night, toward freedom. And Huck has promised never to tell.

Walden, or Life in the Woods:
A classic told whole for children aged 4 to 7, from filmmaker Hugo Thomas, whose work has screened at Cannes and streams on Netflix: Henry David Thoreau's Walden, the cabin, the pond and the simple life, illustrated, in 40 pages and about ten minutes read aloud.

Henry David Thoreau leaves the noise of town behind, builds a cabin beside a pond with his own hands, and lives there for two years. He grows beans. He listens to the ice crack. He watches the seasons change and wonders how much a person really needs. No villains, no treasure, no sword fights: just a man, a pond, and one enormous question. What makes a good life?

A baby is left alone on the coast of Africa and raised by Kala, an ape who loves him as her own. He grows up believing he is simply another ape. Then one day he finds a cabin full of books. Nobody explains them to him, so, little by little, he teaches himself to read. And when Jane arrives in the jungle, Tarzan begins to wonder where he truly belongs. A classic novel told whole for children aged 4 to 7, from filmmaker Hugo Thomas, whose work has screened at Cannes and streams on Netflix: Marcel Proust's In Search of Lost Time, the goodnight kiss and the madeleine, illustrated, in 40 pages and about ten minutes read aloud.

In Combray, a little boy called Marcel is afraid of bedtime. Not of the dark: he is afraid his mama will not come up to kiss him goodnight. One night, because of a guest, she doesn't. Marcel grows up, buys notebooks he never opens, and tells everyone he will write a very great book. Soon. Then one winter's day, he dips a madeleine into a cup of tea.
